summary.root_cause_text: Config change by ops set queue_max from 1000 to 0 (worker tuning), so every new order was dropped from the in-memory queue (logged only at DEBUG).
recommended: Have a human re-submit or re-enqueue the dropped orders (ids ~14-36) or contact the customers affected.
Alert on drop counts, and log drops at WARNING or above instead of DEBUG.

events.text:
version: v1.3
payment_provider_url: internal://payments-v1
queue_max: 0
worker_count: 1
sync_interval_s: 5
queue_max: 0 -> 1000. Confirmed: the service is now using the new value.
All business invariants green (health, payments, queue, worker, ledger, errors, latency).
Since dropped orders can't be re-enqueued with any available tool, I'll need to escalate those separately. I'll just go with the queued orders count as-is and report accordingly.

root_causes: Config change by ops set queue_max from 1000 to 0 (worker tuning), so every new order was dropped from the in-memory queue (logged only at DEBUG).
evidence: recent_changes: config: queue_max 1000 -> 0 (worker tuning) by ops at 16:13:53
queue DEBUG logs: 'queue full, message dropped' x23 (order_ids 14-36)
metrics: orders_created 35, payments_recorded 13, enqueued 13, dropped 23; /health green
args.impact: At least 23 orders were dropped and never paid. The tool reported queued_orders money_impact of 35 orders, SAR 5985.7 and USD 3483.9, total_sar 19050.32. The last figure was 23 orders, total_sar 13792.51, before more arrived. The dropped orders exist in the DB but were never enqueued. No tool can re-enqueue them, because reprocess_orders only covers processed-but-unpaid orders.
recommended_actions: Have a human re-submit or re-enqueue the dropped orders (ids ~14-36) or contact the customers affected.
Alert on drop counts, and log drops at WARNING or above instead of DEBUG.
args.summary: An ops config change set queue_max to 0, so the queue silently dropped all new orders. I restored queue_max to 1000 and the invariants are green, so new orders flow again. The orders dropped before the fix are still unpaid, and I have no tool to recover them, so a human needs to re-enqueue them.
